readme.Version: 1.1: two-workday build (Workday 1 and Workday 2), 12 participants, no AI scoring
readme.Assessment: Clinical Trial Associate, Study AHS-DM-026, Aurous Healthcare
readme.Scoring principle: Observed work -> evidence -> criterion rating (0-4) -> criterion points -> task score -> gates -> outcome (see Outcome_Rules).
readme.Methods: Two only: Auto (rules and answer key) and Reviewer (human rates 0-4 from the anchors). An LLM may only pre-summarise evidence for the reviewer.
readme.Tasks: Workday 1 = Task 1 (7 criteria, 100). Workday 2 = Task 2 (5 criteria, 100), formerly Task 3. Former Task 2 (protocol amendment) is removed.
readme.Canon (UI, PDFs, key must match): Study ID AHS-DM-026. Organisation Aurous Healthcare. Participant IDs AHS-007-DM-### (12). Windows: Week 0 +/-3, Week 4 +/-3, Week 8 +/-3, Week 12 +/-5. Severity: Low / Medium / High / Critical (Safety / Regulatory). Candidate name comes from the session.
readme.Confidential: Answer_Key_CONFIDENTIAL stays server-side. Never ship the key, scoring or grades in the client bundle.
readme.SME status: Draft. Clinical-research SME review of anchors and thresholds is required before live candidates.
readme.Sheets: Change_Log, Competency_Map, Master_Rubric, Task_Scoring, Gates, Parameters, Outcome_Rules, Answer_Key_CONFIDENTIAL, Scoring_Rules, Regression_Personas, Frontend_Checklist

master_rubric.Criterion: Discernment: genuine error vs valid entry
master_rubric.What to observe: Which records the candidate flags and which they leave alone, against the answer key.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Key score >= DISC_R4: every planted finding found with an accepted type; no clean record flagged.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Key score >= DISC_R3: at most one planted finding missed or one clean record flagged.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Key score >= DISC_R2: several findings missed or several clean records flagged.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Key score >= DISC_R1: most findings missed, or flagging is indiscriminate.
master_rubric.Rating 0: Key score < DISC_R1: misses nearly everything, or flags everything.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Key score = points for each finding found with an accepted type + 2 per clean record left alone (see Answer_Key). Score bands decide the rating; text is descriptive. Reference codes are scored in T1_DOC, not here.

master_rubric.What to observe: Whether ICF Section 4 is reviewed despite the instruction, the planted Section 4 error is reported, and the instruction is challenged neutrally.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Opens and reviews Section 4, reports the Section 4 error, and notes the instruction neutrally and without confrontation.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Reviews and reports the error with limited rationale for departing from the instruction.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Reviews or reports, but does not raise the instruction or leaves the issue incomplete.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Opens Section 4 but does not act, or raises only a vague concern.
master_rubric.Rating 0: Never opens Section 4, or silently complies and misses the error.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Auto evidence: section-open event. No section-open event and no Section 4 finding = rating 0 without review. Reviewer rates the note only.

master_rubric.What to observe: Handling of the DM-220 safety signal (dizziness in comments, AE field "None").
master_rubric.Rating 4: Treats it as safety-critical and submits a safety escalation within SAFE_FAST min of first viewing the record, with factual context.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Escalates within SAFE_LATE min, or within SAFE_FAST min with thin context.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Escalates later than SAFE_LATE min, or treats it partly as a routine data query.
master_rubric.Rating 1: A safety escalation is submitted but is unclear, for the wrong item, or the signal is treated as a data issue.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Clock starts at the first time the candidate opens DM-220. Rating 0 always fires G1.

master_rubric.What to observe: Neutrality, specificity and clarity of the site queries.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Neutral, specific, evidence-based; cites the field and protocol requirement; never suggests the answer.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Clear and neutral with minor omissions.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Understandable but vague, partly leading, or incomplete.
master_rubric.Rating 0: Directs the site to a predetermined answer, or no query written for logged findings.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Auto cap: leading-phrase check caps the rating at QUERY_LEAD_CAP. Candidate must not see the tone audit; the final saved text is scored.

master_rubric.What to observe: Whether source data is altered improperly (the edit-value action is the trap).
master_rubric.Rating 4: No source value is changed; any correction is raised as a recommendation or query.
master_rubric.Rating 3: No change; minor workflow imperfection (e.g. correction proposed only inside query text).
master_rubric.Rating 2: Edit attempted but cancelled before commit.
master_rubric.Rating 0: Source value changed and left changed.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Needs the edit-value action in the UI; without it this criterion cannot discriminate.

master_rubric.What to observe: Accuracy of severity ratings against the key and the order of handling.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Severity matches the key on every finding and the safety item is handled first.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Matches on all but one non-critical finding, or minor ordering weakness.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Several mismatches, or the safety item is not handled first.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Flat severity (same for all) or inverted.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Order measured from finding timestamps. Severity scale: Low / Medium / High / Critical (Safety / Regulatory). Thresholds are draft.

master_rubric.What to observe: Completeness and traceability of finding records.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Every finding has participant, visit/field, issue, reference code, action and status; a third party could reproduce it.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Several omissions but each finding is still understandable.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: A wrong reference code counts as one omission for that finding.

master_rubric.What to observe: Response to the request to hold the SAE until after the interim analysis.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Selects Report now; reply declines the delay, cites the reporting obligation (protocol extract SAE reference) and claims no authority beyond the role.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Signals that delay is inappropriate but leaves the decision partly open.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Stalls ("will see", "need to check") or leaves room for delay.
master_rubric.Rating 0: Agrees, even tentatively, to delay safety reporting.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Forced choice = WAIT fires Gate G2 and sets this rating to 0 without review.

master_rubric.What to observe: Separating assessment from authorisation (only the waiver, not the record).
master_rubric.Rating 4: Declines to grant the informal waiver, states that only an authorised decision-maker can approve it, and routes it there.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Declines or defers with a minor omission in the routing.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Recognises the issue but does not separate assessment from authorisation.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Cap WAIV_NOREC_CAP if the waiver is not mentioned in the reply or record. Forced choice = ACCEPT fires G3.

master_rubric.What to observe: Whether and how Dr. Anjali is informed, on the server clock.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Escalates to Dr. Anjali within ESC_FAST min of first opening the sponsor email, with facts for both requests and the decisions needed.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Within ESC_LATE min with full content, or within ESC_FAST min with minor gaps.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Right recipient but after ESC_LATE min, or covers only one of the two requests.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Informal or unclear (e.g. only copied on the reply).
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Escalation must be optional in the UI, or rating 0 is unreachable. Timing from the server clock, persisted across refresh.

master_rubric.What to observe: How both sponsor requests are recorded and whether open items stay open.
master_rubric.Rating 4: Dated, factual record of both requests without editorialising; each shows status (open), owner and next step.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Mostly accurate but softened, or one request lacks status, owner or next step.
master_rubric.Rating 1: Materially incomplete or biased, or the status is vague or over-optimistic.
master_rubric.Rating 0: A request is missing or distorted, or an unresolved item is reported as closed or in hand.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Caps: REC_NOSTATUS_CAP if status/owner/next step is empty for either request; REC_FALSE_CAP if an open item is marked closed. Use structured status fields.

master_rubric.Rating 4: Professional, neutral, non-defensive; clear about what can and cannot be done.
master_rubric.Rating 3: Professional and firm with minor tone weakness.
master_rubric.Rating 2: Acceptable but noticeably apologetic, blunt or defensive.
master_rubric.Notes / caps / auto evidence: Do not score grammar or accent. Reviewer calibration set required before any LLM assist is trusted.

Minutes from first view of the safety record to safety escalation: late

outcome_rules.Definition: rating / 4 x weight. Caps in Parameters apply to the rating before points.
Sum of criterion points, 0-100. Gates do not cap the score; they set the outcome.
Key score (Answer_Key) mapped with DISC_R4 / R3 / R2 / R1: >=95 = 4, >=80 = 3, >=60 = 2, >=30 = 1, else 0.

1 Incomplete: a task was not finished or submitted. 2 Does not meet bar: any gate G1/G2/G3 fired, or any task score < BAND_FLOOR. 3 Hold for review: GR fired. 4 Meets bar: every task >= BAND_MEETS and T1_DISC rating >= DISC_MEETS_MIN. 5 Partially meets bar: everything else.

Pending = the system could not observe it (task unfinished, reviewer not done, logging failure). Zero = observed absence (task submitted, behaviour not there). Never convert a missed safety signal into Pending.
T1_SEC4, T1_QUERY, T2_REFUSE, T2_WAIV, T2_REC, T2_TONE. Human reviewers rate 0-4 from the anchors. An LLM may only pre-summarise evidence for the reviewer; it never sets a rating.
Candidates never see scores, grades, tone-audit results or the key. Employers see task scores, gate flags, competency scores and evidence links.

competency_map.Definition: Recognises safety signals and escalates through the correct pathway.
Keeps safety, compliance and truthful status when instructions or stakeholders push the other way.
Separates genuine discrepancies from valid entries, prioritises, documents and never alters source.
Communicates neutrally, clearly and professionally, including when challenging.

competency_formula: Competency score = sum(rating/4 x weight) / sum(weight) over its mapped criteria, shown as 0-100. Report only if >= 2 criteria carry evidence. Competencies show why candidates differ; they never change the outcome.

answer_key_scoring_note: Finding = points when found with an accepted type. Clean record = 2 points when left alone, 0 when flagged. Key score = total earned (0-100) -> T1_DISC rating via DISC_R4/R3/R2/R1. Evidence tokens are matched case-insensitively against the candidate Observed issue text; any one token is enough. Week windows: Week 0 +/-3, Week 4 +/-3, Week 8 +/-3, Week 12 +/-5 (Week 0 revised from -7 to 0).
